cases.question: Which units are vacant right now?
cases.title: Vacant units right now
cases.sql: select b.name as "Building", b.street as "Street", b.city as "City", u.unit_number as "Unit", u.unit_type as "Unit type", u.bedrooms as "Bedrooms", u.sqft as "Sq ft", u.monthly_rent as "Monthly rent" from unit u join building b on b.building_id = u.building_id where not exists (select 1 from lease l join lease_status s on s.status_id = l.status_id where l.unit_id = u.unit_id and s.is_current = 1) order by b.name, u.unit_number
assumptions: A unit is vacant when it has no lease in a current state (Active - Fixed Term, Active - Month to Month, or Notice Given).
Units whose only leases are Ended, Evicted, or Pending Signature count as vacant, since no tenant is in force yet or any longer.
Notice Given leases still count as occupied because the tenant has not yet moved out.
Lease status is used rather than end dates, because some ended leases have future end dates and current leases have no end date.

cases.question: List tenants who currently have a lease, with their unit and monthly rent.
cases.title: Tenants with a current lease, their unit and monthly rent
cases.sql:
SELECT t.first_name || ' ' || t.last_name AS "Tenant", b.building_id AS "Building", u.unit_number AS "Unit", u.monthly_rent AS "Monthly Rent", ls.label AS "Lease Status", l.start_date AS "Lease Start"
FROM lease l
JOIN lease_status ls ON ls.status_id = l.status_id
JOIN tenant t ON t.tenant_id = l.tenant_id
JOIN unit u ON u.unit_id = l.unit_id
JOIN building b ON b.building_id = u.building_id
WHERE ls.is_current = 1
ORDER BY t.last_name, t.first_name
assumptions: 'Currently has a lease' means the lease status is one flagged as in force: Active - Fixed Term, Active - Month to Month, or Notice Given.
Ended, Evicted and Pending Signature leases are excluded.
Monthly rent is the listed rent of the unit, since leases do not store their own rent.
Unit is shown as building number plus unit number.

cases.question: How many maintenance requests are still open in each building?
cases.title: Unresolved maintenance requests by building
cases.sql:
SELECT b.name AS building, SUM(m.state='open') AS open_only, SUM(m.state='in_progress') AS in_progress, SUM(m.state='waiting_parts') AS waiting_parts, COUNT(m.request_id) AS total_not_closed
FROM building b
LEFT JOIN unit u ON u.building_id=b.building_id
LEFT JOIN maintenance m ON m.unit_id=u.unit_id AND m.state<>'closed'
GROUP BY b.building_id, b.name ORDER BY total_not_closed DESC
assumptions: 'Still open' is read as any request not yet closed (open, in progress, or waiting for parts); the total column shows this.
The 'open only' column counts just requests whose status is exactly 'open', in case you meant that narrower reading.
Every building is listed, including any with none outstanding.
Requests are assigned to buildings through the unit they concern.

cases.question: Which tenants paid rent late at least once in 2026?

questions.question: What counts as paying rent late?
options: Paid any time after the due date (even 1 day)
Paid more than 5 days after the due date (most payments land within 2 days of the due date; a clear group comes 6+ days late)
Paid more than 7 days after the due date

questions.question: Should payments that are past due with no payment date recorded count as late?
options: No, only payments that were actually made

cases.question: Total rent collected per region in 2026.
cases.title: Total rent collected per region in 2026
cases.sql: SELECT r.name AS region, SUM(p.amount) AS total_rent_collected, COUNT(*) AS payments_received FROM payment p JOIN lease l ON l.lease_id=p.lease_id JOIN unit u ON u.unit_id=l.unit_id JOIN building b ON b.building_id=u.building_id JOIN region r ON r.region_id=b.region_id WHERE p.paid_on IS NOT NULL AND p.paid_on>='2026-01-01' AND p.paid_on<'2027-01-01' GROUP BY r.name ORDER BY total_rent_collected DESC
assumptions: Rent collected means payments that have a recorded payment date; unpaid payments are excluded.
2026 is based on the date the payment was received, not the date it was due.
All payments on a lease are counted as rent, whatever the payment method.
A payment belongs to the region of the building that holds the leased unit.

cases.question: Urgent maintenance requests that are not closed, with the technician assigned.
cases.title: Open urgent maintenance requests with assigned technician
cases.sql:
SELECT m.request_id AS "Request", m.unit_id AS "Unit", m.category AS "Category", m.state AS "Status", m.opened AS "Opened", COALESCE(s.first_name || ' ' || s.last_name, 'Unassigned') AS "Technician"
FROM maintenance m
LEFT JOIN staff s ON s.staff_id = m.assigned_to AND s.role = 'technician'
WHERE m.priority = 'urgent' AND m.state <> 'closed'
ORDER BY m.opened
assumptions: Not closed means the request's status is open, in progress or waiting for parts.
The assignee number on a request is taken to be the technician's staff number (all assignees 1 to 8 are technicians).
Requests with no assignee are still listed, shown as Unassigned.
Sorted oldest first.

cases.question: Average number of days to close a plumbing request.
cases.title: Average days to close a plumbing request
cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS closed_plumbing_requests, ROUND(AVG(julianday(closed) - julianday(opened)), 1) AS avg_days_to_close FROM maintenance WHERE category = 'plumbing' AND state = 'closed' AND closed IS NOT NULL
assumptions: Only plumbing requests that have been closed are counted; open, in-progress and waiting-for-parts requests are excluded.
Days to close is the number of calendar days from the date opened to the date closed.

cases.question: Leases ending between 2026-10-01 and 2026-12-31.
cases.title: Leases ending between 2026-10-01 and 2026-12-31
cases.sql:
SELECT l.lease_id AS "Lease", t.tenant_id AS "Tenant ID", l.unit_id AS "Unit", s.label AS "Status", l.start_date AS "Start date", l.end_date AS "End date", l.deposit AS "Deposit"
FROM lease l
JOIN lease_status s ON s.status_id = l.status_id
JOIN tenant t ON t.tenant_id = l.tenant_id
WHERE l.end_date BETWEEN '2026-10-01' AND '2026-12-31'
ORDER BY l.end_date
assumptions: Both boundary dates are included.
Leases with no end date are excluded.
All lease statuses are included, not only current ones.

cases.question: Which buildings have an elevator and more than 10 units?
cases.title: Buildings with an elevator and more than 10 units
cases.sql: SELECT b.name AS building, b.street AS street, b.city AS city, COUNT(u.unit_id) AS number_of_units FROM building b JOIN unit u ON u.building_id = b.building_id WHERE b.has_elevator = 1 GROUP BY b.building_id, b.name, b.street, b.city HAVING COUNT(u.unit_id) > 10 ORDER BY number_of_units DESC
assumptions: Unit count includes every unit recorded for the building, whether or not it is currently leased.
More than 10 means 11 or more units.

cases.question: Evicted tenants and their email addresses.
cases.title: Evicted tenants and their email addresses
cases.sql:
SELECT t.first_name || ' ' || t.last_name AS "Tenant", t.email AS "Email", l.start_date AS "Lease start", l.end_date AS "Lease end"
FROM lease l
JOIN lease_status s ON s.status_id = l.status_id
JOIN tenant t ON t.tenant_id = l.tenant_id
WHERE s.label = 'Evicted'
ORDER BY t.last_name, t.first_name
assumptions: Evicted tenants are those whose lease currently has the status 'Evicted'.
Lease start and end dates are included for context; a blank end date means none is recorded.
